from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title_text = "Introduction: The Factorial Machine"
        lines = [
            "Meet Facto, our machine that calculates factorials.",
            "Factorials multiply all integers down to one.",
            "Three factorial is three times two times one.",
            "But what happens when Facto reaches zero?",
            "Zero factorial seems like a mystery."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Meet Facto, our machine that calculates factorials.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # Subtitle
        subtitle = Text("The Mystery of 0!", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_in_area(subtitle, "A1", "A6")
        
        # Facto Robot Design
        body = Rectangle(width=2.2, height=1.6, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=1)
        label = Text("Facto", color=BLACK, weight=BOLD, font_size=24).shift(DOWN * 0.4)
        eye_l = Circle(radius=0.18, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1).shift(UP * 0.3 + LEFT * 0.4)
        eye_r = Circle(radius=0.18, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1).shift(UP * 0.3 + RIGHT * 0.4)
        pupil_l = Dot(radius=0.08, color=BLACK).move_to(eye_l.get_center())
        pupil_r = Dot(radius=0.08, color=BLACK).move_to(eye_r.get_center())
        
        facto = VGroup(body, label, eye_l, eye_r, pupil_l, pupil_r)
        self.place_in_area(facto, "C3", "D4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(subtitle))
        self.play(FadeIn(facto))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Factorials multiply all integers down to one.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        # Fixed FileNotFoundError: Replace MathTex with Text to avoid dependency on missing latex executable
        formula = Text("n! = n × (n-1) × ... × 1", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "B1", "B6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Three factorial is three times two times one.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # 3! animation
        three_fact = Text("3!", color="#00FF00", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(three_fact, "D1")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(three_fact))
        self.play(three_fact.animate.move_to(facto.get_center()))
        
        process_3 = Text("3 × 2 × 1", color="#00FF00", font_size=28)
        self.place_in_area(process_3, "C3", "C4") 
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(three_fact, process_3))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        out_6 = Text("6", color="#00FF00", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(out_6, "D6")
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(process_3, out_6))
        self.play(out_6.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.5), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(out_6))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # But what happens when Facto reaches zero?
        
        # 2!
        two_fact = Text("2!", color="#00FF00", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(two_fact, "D1")
        out_2 = Text("2", color="#00FF00", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(out_2, "D6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(two_fact))
        self.play(two_fact.animate.move_to(facto.get_center()), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(two_fact, out_2), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(FadeOut(out_2), run_time=0.4)
        
        # 1!
        one_fact = Text("1!", color="#00FF00", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(one_fact, "D1")
        out_1 = Text("1", color="#00FF00", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(out_1, "D6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(one_fact))
        self.play(one_fact.animate.move_to(facto.get_center()), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(one_fact, out_1), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(FadeOut(out_1), run_time=0.4)
        
        # Transition to 0!
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF0000")
        zero_fact = Text("0!", color="#FF0000", font_size=40)
        self.place_at_grid(zero_fact, "D1")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(zero_fact))
        self.play(zero_fact.animate.move_to(facto.get_center()))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Zero factorial seems like a mystery.
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF0000")
        
        # Confusion eyes
        q_mark_l = Text("?", color="#FF0000", font_size=44).move_to(eye_l.get_center())
        q_mark_r = Text("?", color="#FF0000", font_size=44).move_to(eye_r.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(pupil_l, pupil_r),
            FadeIn(q_mark_l, q_mark_r),
            facto[0].animate.set_stroke(color="#FF0000", width=4)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Layout - Title
        title = Text("The Logic of Factorials", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        # 2. Left side - Lecture Content
        lecture_lines = [
            "- What is a Factorial?",
            "- The Pattern: n! = n × (n-1)!",
            "- Dividing by n: (n-1)! = n! / n",
            "- If n=1, then 0! = 1! / 1",
            "- Therefore, 0! = 1"
        ]
        
        lecture_vgroup = VGroup(*[
            Text(line, font_size=24, color=WHITE) 
            for line in lecture_lines
        ]).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        
        lecture_vgroup.scale(0.85).to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.8)

        # 3. Right side - Grid/Visualization Area
        # Creating a coordinate system for the right side
        grid_origin = RIGHT * 3 + DOWN * 0.5
        factorial_table = VGroup(
            Text("4! = 24", font_size=28),
            Text("3! = 6", font_size=28),
            Text("2! = 2", font_size=28),
            Text("1! = 1", font_size=28),
            Text("0! = 1", font_size=28, color=YELLOW)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5).move_to(grid_origin)

        # 4. Animations
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(0.5)

        for line in lecture_vgroup:
            self.play(FadeIn(line, shift=RIGHT * 0.2), run_time=0.8)
        
        self.wait(1)

        self.play(Create(SurroundingRectangle(lecture_vgroup[2], color=BLUE)))
        
        self.play(
            AnimationGroup(
                *[FadeIn(item, shift=UP * 0.3) for item in factorial_table],
                lag_ratio=0.3
            )
        )
        
        self.play(Indicate(factorial_table[-1]))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize layout
        self.setup_layout("The Algebraic Proof", [
            "Use the formula: n! equals n times (n-1)!",
            "Let n equal one to check the math.",
            "This equation forces zero factorial to equal one."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        EMERALD = "#50C878"
        GOLD = "#FFD700"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(EMERALD))
        
        # Fixed: Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency error
        formula = Text("n! = n × (n - 1)!", color=EMERALD)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(EMERALD))
        
        # Step: Transform n to 1
        formula_sub = Text("1! = 1 × (1 - 1)!", color=EMERALD)
        self.place_in_area(formula_sub, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(Transform(formula, formula_sub))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Step: Simplify the parenthesis: 1 = 1 * 0!
        formula_simp = Text("1 = 1 × 0!", color=EMERALD)
        self.place_in_area(formula_simp, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(Transform(formula, formula_simp))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GOLD))
        
        # Step: Divide both sides by 1 to isolate 0!
        formula_final = Text("1 = 0!", color=EMERALD)
        self.place_in_area(formula_final, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(Transform(formula, formula_final))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Flip to 0! = 1 for clarity
        formula_ordered = Text("0! = 1", color=EMERALD)
        self.place_in_area(formula_ordered, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.8)
        self.play(Transform(formula, formula_ordered))
        
        # Surround with glowing gold box
        box = SurroundingRectangle(formula, color=GOLD, buff=0.3, stroke_width=4)
        glow = box.copy().set_stroke(width=8, opacity=0.3)
        
        self.play(Create(box), FadeIn(glow))
        self.play(Indicate(formula, color=GOLD))
        self.wait(3)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with specific lines
        lines = [
            "Factorials count how many ways to arrange objects.",
            "Three objects have six arrangements; one has one.",
            "An empty shelf has exactly one arrangement."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Combinatorial Perspective (Arrangements)", lines)

        # Helper for a simple hat shape
        def create_hat(color="#FF00FF"):
            brim = Line(LEFT * 0.4, RIGHT * 0.4, stroke_width=4, color=color)
            top = Arc(radius=0.25, start_angle=0, angle=PI, stroke_width=4, color=color).shift(UP * 0.05)
            return VGroup(brim, top)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )

        # Display 3 distinct magenta hats (#FF00FF)
        hats = VGroup(create_hat(), create_hat(), create_hat())
        # Position hats on a virtual shelf line
        self.place_at_grid(hats[0], "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(hats[1], "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(hats[2], "B4", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Display the number '6' ($3!$) - Changed to Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        arrangements_text = Text("6 (3!)", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(arrangements_text, "C3", scale_factor=1.2)

        self.play(FadeIn(hats), Write(arrangements_text))
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )

        # Remove all hats leaving an empty shelf
        # The shelf is a line at the same row D
        shelf = Line(self.grid["D1"], self.grid["D5"], stroke_width=4, color=GREY_B)
        
        # Display text '1 Way' (#00FFFF) next to the empty shelf
        one_way_text = Text("1 Way", color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(one_way_text, "E3", scale_factor=1.2)

        # Animation transition: hats and 3! fade out, shelf and "1 Way" appear
        self.play(
            FadeOut(hats),
            FadeOut(arrangements_text),
            Create(shelf)
        )
        self.play(Write(one_way_text))
        self.wait(4)

        # Final state
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Mystery of 0!", 
            [
                "- Recursive Definition",
                "- Division Property",
                "- Mathematical Consistency"
            ]
        )

        # 2. Mathematical Content
        # Fixed FileNotFoundError: 'latex' by using Text with unicode characters 
        # instead of MathTex, which requires a LaTeX installation.
        formula_1 = Text("n! = n × (n - 1)!", color=WHITE, font_size=36)
        formula_2 = Text("1! = 1 × (1 - 1)!", color=BLUE, font_size=36)
        formula_3 = Text("1 = 1 × 0!", color=YELLOW, font_size=36)
        formula_4 = Text("0! = 1", color=GREEN, font_size=36)

        # 3. Placement and Animation
        self.place_at_grid(formula_1, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula_1))
        self.wait(1)

        self.place_at_grid(formula_2, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        # TransformMatchingShapes works well with Text as it matches individual characters
        self.play(TransformMatchingShapes(formula_1.copy(), formula_2))
        self.wait(1)

        self.place_at_grid(formula_3, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula_3))
        self.wait(1)

        self.place_at_grid(formula_4, "E3", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Indicate(formula_4), Create(SurroundingRectangle(formula_4, color=YELLOW)))
        self.wait(3)

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        """Initializes the background and lecture sidebar."""
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        
        # Title
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Sidebar content
        lecture_vgroup = VGroup(*[
            Text(line, font_size=20, color=GREY_A) for line in lecture_lines
        ]).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        
        lecture_vgroup.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.7).shift(UP * 0.5)
        self.add(lecture_vgroup)

        # Grid system for right-side content
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Calculate coordinates favoring the right side
                x_coord = 1.5 + (j * 1.2)
                y_coord = 2.5 - (i * 1.2)
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x_coord, y_coord, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        """Utility to place mobjects on the defined layout grid."""
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        if grid_pos in self.grid:
            mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        else:
            mobject.move_to(RIGHT * 3)

sections.title: Introduction: The Factorial Machine
sections.content: Introduce the concept of factorials (n!) as a 'product of descending integers.' Use a visual 'Factorial Machine' character named 'Facto' that takes a number and spits out the result of the multiplication. Define the prerequisite knowledge: n! = n * (n-1) * (n-2)... * 1.
sections.example: Facto the Robot processes 3!: He grabs 3, 2, and 1, multiplies them, and outputs 6. He then processes 2! to get 2, and 1! to get 1. But then he encounters 0! and looks confused.

sections.title: The Pattern Approach (Division Logic)
sections.content: Present a table of factorials in descending order. Instead of multiplying to go down, show the logic of dividing by the current number to find the previous factorial value. This establishes a predictable mathematical rhythm.
sections.example: Display a staircase: 4! is 24. To get 3!, divide 24 by 4 (= 6). To get 2!, divide 6 by 3 (= 2). To get 1!, divide 2 by 2 (= 1). To find 0!, follow the pattern: divide 1 (the value of 1!) by 1. The result is 1.

sections.title: The Algebraic Proof
sections.content: Introduce the recursive formula n! = n * (n-1)!. This is the fundamental rule of factorials. Explain that for this rule to remain consistent for all positive integers, the value of 0! must be specifically defined.
sections.example: Write the equation 1! = 1 * (1 - 1)!. This simplifies to 1 = 1 * 0!. To make this equation true, 0! must equal 1. Visual: A balance scale where '1' is on one side and '1 * 0!' is on the other.

sections.title: The Combinatorial Perspective (Arrangements)
sections.content: Explain factorials as the number of ways to arrange objects. This is a shift from pure calculation to logic. Ask: 'How many ways can you arrange zero items?'
sections.example: Three hats can be arranged in 6 ways (3!). Two hats in 2 ways (2!). One hat in 1 way (1!). If you have an empty shelf (0 hats), there is exactly 'one way' to have it: keeping it empty. In combinatorics, 'doing nothing' counts as one distinct arrangement.

sections.title: Conclusion: Why it Matters
sections.content: Summarize the three proofs (Pattern, Algebra, Logic). Explain that 0! = 1 isn't just a quirk; it's a necessary definition that allows complex formulas like the Binomial Theorem and Taylor Series to function without breaking.
sections.example: Show a 'Mathematical Puzzle' where 0! = 1 is the missing piece that makes the whole picture of Calculus and Probability fit together perfectly. Facto the Robot smiles, his 'confusion' light turns off.

storyboard.title: Introduction: The Factorial Machine
lecture_lines: Meet Facto, our machine that calculates factorials.
Factorials multiply all integers down to one.
Three factorial is three times two times one.
But what happens when Facto reaches zero?
Zero factorial seems like a mystery.
animations: Write 'The Mystery of $0!$' in white (#FFFFFF) at the top.
Create a gold box (#FFD700) labeled 'Facto' with eyes [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg].
Animate '3!' entering Facto [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg], then '3 * 2 * 1' appearing, then '6' exiting.
Quickly repeat for '2! -> 2' and '1! -> 1' using Facto [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg].
Animate '0!' entering Facto [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg], and Facto's eyes changing to red question marks (#FF0000).

storyboard.title: The Pattern Approach (Division Logic)
lecture_lines: Let's look at factorials in a descending pattern.
To find three factorial, divide twenty-four by four.
Next, we divide by three to reach two factorial.
Dividing by two leads us to one factorial.
Dividing one by one reveals zero factorial equals one.
animations: Draw a green arrow (#00FF00) from 24 to 6 labeled 'divided by 4'.
Draw a green arrow (#00FF00) from 6 to 2 labeled 'divided by 3'.
Draw a green arrow (#00FF00) from 2 to 1 labeled 'divided by 2'.
Draw a final arrow labeled 'divided by 1' pointing to a new line: $0! = 1$ in yellow (#FFFF00).

storyboard.title: The Algebraic Proof
lecture_lines: Any factorial equals n times its predecessor.
Let us substitute n with the number one.
Simplifying gives one equals one times zero factorial.
Isolating zero factorial shows it must be one.
This formula confirms zero factorial equals one logically.
animations: Write $n! = n \times (n-1)!$ in emerald (#50C878) at center.
Transform $n$ to $1$: $1! = 1 \times (1-1)!$.
Simplify the parenthesis: $1 = 1 \times 0!$.
Divide both sides by $1$ to isolate $0!$.
Surround $0! = 1$ with a glowing gold box (#FFD700).

storyboard.title: The Combinatorial Perspective (Arrangements)
lecture_lines: Factorials count how many ways to arrange objects.
Three objects have six arrangements; one has one.
An empty shelf has exactly one arrangement.
animations: Display 3 distinct magenta hats (#FF00FF) and the number '6' ($3!$).
Remove all hats leaving an empty shelf.
Display text '1 Way' (#00FFFF) next to the empty shelf.

storyboard.title: Conclusion: Why it Matters
lecture_lines: Zero factorial as one keeps mathematics consistent.
It enables complex formulas in calculus and probability.
Our mystery is solved, and Facto is satisfied.
animations: Show a complex formula (e.g., $e^x = \sum \frac{x^n}{n!}$) in light blue (#ADD8E6) highlighting the $n!$ denominator.
Show Facto the Robot [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] (#FFD700) smiling.
Fade in final text '$0! = 1$ completes the pattern.' in white (#FFFFFF).
